newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures ended the week near a contract high amid a favourable combination of a stronger franc, good demand from domestic and overseas investors and a renewed conviction monetary union will go ahead in 1999.
The December bond future settled at 124.20, close to the contract high of 124.26 which it touched several times during Friday's session, outpacing the Bund future.

December PIBOR also outperformed Euromarks to reach a new contract high at 96.27. It was boosted by a call money easing early on Friday and a franc rally which took the currency to 3.3873 per mark, its highest level for two months.

Traders said the French budget unveiled this week along with the cut in the intervention rate on Thursday had given French markets a boost. "There's now a strong consensus that European monetary union is in the bag," said a bond trader.

Francois-Xavier Chauchat, economist at Banque Nationale de Paris, said despite the tricks used to get the French budget down to three percent of gross domestic product, it "reinforced the economic credibility of monetary union."
Traders said the bond market may decline at the beginning of next week ahead of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy meeting on Tuesday, but any losses would be limited.

The renewed conviction that monetary union will go ahead sent the franc surging to its two-month high. Traders said volume in Mark/Paris was three times as high as usual with some investors closing out large short franc positions, triggering a series of stops.
The franc was trading at 3.3886 GMT at 1545 GMT, up from Thursday's low of 3.4090 and September's low of 3.4315 per mark.

The favourable mood in French markets allowed the French Treasury to sell an extra 2.477 billion francs of BTANs, after selling 17.87 billion on Thursday. Both the two- and five-year spreads over German narrowed two basis points on Friday.
